title: Polynomials
notes: Degree 1 = linear polynomial (ax+b), degree 2 = quadratic (ax^2+bx+c), degree 3 = cubic (ax^3+bx^2+cx+d), a not 0 in each.
A real number k is a zero of p(x) if p(k) = 0.
Zeroes of p(x) = x-coordinates of the points where the graph y = p(x) cuts the x-axis.
Linear polynomial: exactly ONE zero (graph is a straight line, crosses x-axis once).
Quadratic polynomial: graph is a parabola. It can cut the x-axis at 2 points (2 distinct zeroes), touch it at 1 point (2 equal zeroes), or not touch it at all (no real zero). Max 2 zeroes.
Cubic polynomial: max 3 zeroes -- graph crosses x-axis at most 3 times.
General rule: a polynomial of degree n has at most n zeroes.
Relationship between zeroes and coefficients is the most-tested idea in this chapter -- learn both quadratic and cubic versions cold.

formulas.formula: alpha + beta = -b/a = -(Coefficient of x)/(Coefficient of x^2)

formulas.name: Product of zeroes (quadratic)
formulas.formula: alpha * beta = c/a = (Constant term)/(Coefficient of x^2)

examples.question: Look at given graphs of y = p(x); find the number of zeroes of p(x) for each.
examples.solution: Count how many times each graph touches/crosses the x-axis -- that count is the number of real zeroes (graph-reading exercise, no algebra needed).

examples.question: Find the zeroes of x^2 + 7x + 10 and verify the relationship between zeroes and coefficients.
examples.solution: Factorise: x^2+7x+10 = (x+2)(x+5), zeroes = -2, -5. Sum = -7 = -(7)/1 checks out. Product = 10 = 10/1 checks out.

examples.question: Find the zeroes of x^2 - 3 and verify the relationship.
Find a quadratic polynomial whose sum and product of zeroes are -3 and 2.
examples.solution: Using p(x) = k[x^2-(sum)x+(product)]: x^2 - (-3)x + 2 = x^2 + 3x + 2 (take k=1).

examples.question: Verify that 3, -1, 1/3 are zeroes of 3x^3-5x^2-11x-3 and check the zero-coefficient relations.
examples.solution: Substituting each value gives p(x)=0 in all three cases. Sum = 3-1+1/3 = 5/3 = -b/a. Sum of pairwise products = -11/3 = c/a. Product = 3x(-1)x(1/3) = -1 = -d/a = -(-3)/3.

exercises.question: Graphs of y = p(x) are given for various polynomials p(x). Find the number of zeroes of p(x) in each case.
exercises.answer: Read directly off the graph: count of x-axis intersections = number of zeroes (answers vary per graph, values 0 to 3).

exercises.question: Find the zeroes of the following and verify the relationship between zeroes and coefficients: (i) x^2-2x-8 (ii) 4s^2-4s+1 (iii) 6x^2-3-7x (iv) 4u^2+8u (v) t^2-15 (vi) 3x^2-x-4
Find a quadratic polynomial with the given sum and product of zeroes respectively: (i) 1/4, -1 (ii) root2, 1/3 (iii) 0, root5 (iv) 1, 1 (v) -1/4, 1/4 (vi) 4, 1
